claim: Truncation of the SH3 domain of BIN1 leads to centronuclear myopathy.
source: Truncation of the protein-protein interaction SH3 domain of the membrane remodeling Bridging Integrator 1 (BIN1, Amphiphysin 2) protein leads to centronuclear myopathy.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about BIN1 truncation and CNM.

claim: BIN1 contains an N-terminal BAR domain required for membrane binding.
source: It contains an N-terminal BAR domain required for membrane binding — named after BIN1, AMPH, and RVS167 — and a C-terminal SRC Homology 3 (SH3) domain, required for partner recruitment (Owen et al., 1998; Peter et al., 2004; Prokic et al., 2014).
evidence: This structural information is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: BIN1 contains a C-terminal SH3 domain required for partner recruitment.
source: It contains an N-terminal BAR domain required for membrane binding — named after BIN1, AMPH, and RVS167 — and a C-terminal SRC Homology 3 (SH3) domain, required for partner recruitment (Owen et al., 1998; Peter et al., 2004; Prokic et al., 2014).
evidence: This structural information is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: BAR domain deposition on membrane surfaces causes membrane curvature.
source: BAR domain deposition on membrane surfaces causes membrane curvature and BIN1-mediated membrane remodeling was found to be critical in the formation of various endomembrane structures, such as clathrin- or caveolin-coated vesicles, recycling endosomes, as well as tubular invaginations of the plasma membrane in muscle cells, known as T-tubules (Lee et al., 2002; Ramjaun and McPherson, 1998; Razzaq et al., 2001).
evidence: This mechanism is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: BIN1-mediated membrane remodeling is critical in the formation of clathrin- or caveolin-coated vesicles, recycling endosomes, and T-tubules.
source: BAR domain deposition on membrane surfaces causes membrane curvature and BIN1-mediated membrane remodeling was found to be critical in the formation of various endomembrane structures, such as clathrin- or caveolin-coated vesicles, recycling endosomes, as well as tubular invaginations of the plasma membrane in muscle cells, known as T-tubules (Lee et al., 2002; Ramjaun and McPherson, 1998; Razzaq et al., 2001).
evidence: This functional role is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The BIN1 SH3 domain recruits DNM2 to curved membranes.
source: A well-studied role of the BIN1 SH3 domain is to recruit Dynamin 2 (DNM2) to curved membranes, whose local oligomerization appears to be critical in both membrane fission during vesicle scission and in the formation of T-tubules in muscle cells (Chin et al., 2015; Cowling et al., 2017; David et al., 1996; Fujise et al., 2022; Volchuk et al., 1998; Figure 1A).
evidence: This interaction is supported by multiple citations and referenced in Figure 1A.

claim: DNM2 oligomerization is critical in membrane fission during vesicle scission and in the formation of T-tubules.
source: A well-studied role of the BIN1 SH3 domain is to recruit Dynamin 2 (DNM2) to curved membranes, whose local oligomerization appears to be critical in both membrane fission during vesicle scission and in the formation of T-tubules in muscle cells (Chin et al., 2015; Cowling et al., 2017; David et al., 1996; Fujise et al., 2022; Volchuk et al., 1998; Figure 1A).
evidence: This functional role is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Mutations of DNM2 lead to autosomal dominant centronuclear myopathy.
source: Both BIN1 and DNM2 are implicated in centronuclear myopathy (CNM): mutations of DNM2 were found to lead to autosomal dominant CNM and mutations of BIN1 were found to lead to autosomal recessive CNM (Bitoun et al., 2005; Gómez-Oca et al., 2022; Nicot et al., 2007; Rossi et al., 2022).
evidence: This genetic association is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Mutations of BIN1 lead to autosomal recessive centronuclear myopathy.
source: Both BIN1 and DNM2 are implicated in centronuclear myopathy (CNM): mutations of DNM2 were found to lead to autosomal dominant CNM and mutations of BIN1 were found to lead to autosomal recessive CNM (Bitoun et al., 2005; Gómez-Oca et al., 2022; Nicot et al., 2007; Rossi et al., 2022).
evidence: This genetic association is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Pathological BIN1 mutations in the BAR domain prevent membrane-remodeling function and almost completely abolish BIN1-related cellular mechanisms.
source: Pathological BIN1 mutations located in its BAR domain prevent its membrane-remodeling function, and almost completely abolish BIN1-related cellular mechanisms (Nicot et al., 2007)⁠.
evidence: This functional consequence is supported by a citation.

claim: Truncations of the BIN1 SH3 domain (Q573*, K575*) result in centronuclear myopathy.
source: Importantly, rare truncations of the SH3 domain of BIN1 (caused by early stop codons such as Q573*, or K575*) also result in CNM (Laiman et al., 2023; Nicot et al., 2007).
evidence: This genetic association is supported by citations.

claim: BIN1 variants with truncated SH3 domains maintain membrane remodeling activities but are unable to recruit DNM2.
source: These BIN1 variants – whose BAR domains are intact – maintain their membrane remodeling activities, such as creating tubular membrane structures, yet are unable to recruit DNM2.
evidence: This functional characterization is stated as a known property of these variants.

claim: A frameshift mutation causing a 52-residue hydrophobic extension of the BIN1 SH3 domain causes autosomal dominant centronuclear myopathy.
source: In addition, a frameshift mutation causing a mostly hydrophobic 52-residue extension of the BIN1 SH3 domain was found to cause autosomal dominant CNM (Böhm et al., 2014)⁠.
evidence: This genetic association is supported by a citation.

claim: Exogenous expression of BIN1 is a promising therapeutic approach to treat different genetic forms of CNM.
source: Exogenous expression of BIN1 is a promising therapeutic approach to treat different genetic forms of CNM, reinforcing the importance of characterizing the interactions of BIN1 and their functional consequences (Lionello et al., 2022; Lionello et al., 2019).
evidence: This therapeutic potential is supported by citations.

claim: SH3 domains recognize proline-rich motifs, most typically basic PxxP motifs.
source: SH3 domains recognize Proline-rich motifs (PRMs), most typically basic PxxP motifs (Lim et al., 1994;⁠ Figure 1B).
evidence: This molecular recognition property is supported by a citation and Figure 1B.

claim: DNM2 contains an extensive proline-rich region in its C-terminal tail including a series of putative PRMs that interact with the BIN1 SH3 domain.
source: DNM2 contains an extensive Proline-rich region (PRR) in its C-terminal tail including a series of putative PRMs that are thought to interact with the SH3 domain of BIN1 (Grabs et al., 1997)⁠.
evidence: This structural feature is supported by a citation.

claim: SH3 domains are typically highly promiscuous and can bind to hundreds of partners.
source: However, SH3 domains are typically highly promiscuous and can bind to hundreds of partners, similarly to other protein-protein interaction domain families (Gogl et al., 2022; Wu et al., 2007).
evidence: This property of SH3 domains is supported by citations.

claim: MYC, TAU, RIN3, and CAVIN4 are SH3-mediated interaction partners of BIN1.
source: So far, only a handful of other SH3-mediated interactions of BIN1 were identified, such as MYC, TAU, RIN3, and Caveolae-associated protein 4 (CAVIN4) (Andresen et al., 2012; Kajiho et al., 2003; Lasorsa et al., 2018; Lo et al., 2021; Malki et al., 2017; Pineda-Lucena et al., 2005)⁠.
evidence: These interactions are supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Viral proteins interact with the BIN1 SH3 domain.
source: Viral proteins were also found to interact with the BIN1 SH3 domain (Nanda et al., 2006; Tossavainen et al., 2016).
evidence: These interactions are supported by citations.

claim: The interactome of full-length BIN1 was screened in multiple high-throughput interactomic studies.
source: In addition to these interactions of the BIN1 SH3 domain identified with low-throughput approaches, the interactome of full-length (FL) BIN1 was also screened in multiple high-throughput interactomic studies (Cho et al., 2022; Ellis et al., 2012; Huttlin et al., 2021; Luck et al., 2020)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The results of high-throughput interactomic studies of BIN1 overlapped poorly.
source: However, the results of these studies overlapped poorly (Figure 1C).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: The BIN1 variants Y531S, D537V, and F584S do not detectably bind to the PRR of DNM2.
source: The holdup assay revealed that the variants Y531S, D537V, and F584S do not detectably bind to the PRR of DNM2, while the other variants display affinities similar to the WT BIN1.
evidence: This is based on experimental holdup assay data presented in the study.

claim: The Y531F and D537A artificial mutations cause marked loss of DNM2 binding activity.
source: In agreement with these findings, artificial point mutations were used to map the DNM2 binding interface on BIN1 in the past and two studied mutations, Y531F and D537A coinciding with Y531S and D537V natural variants, were also found to cause a marked loss of DNM2 binding activity (Owen et al., 1998)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: CNM-causing BIN1 variants are unable to recruit DNM2 to BIN1-induced membrane invaginations.
source: Clinically important, CNM-causing BIN1 variants were previously found to be unable to recruit DNM2 to BIN1-induced membrane invaginations that resemble T-tubules (Nicot et al., 2007)⁠.
evidence: This cellular phenotype is supported by a citation.

claim: All tested BIN1 variants are capable of promoting tubular endomembrane structures.
source: As expected, all tested BIN1 variants were capable of promoting tubular endomembrane structures since this process is mediated by the BAR domain of BIN1 and not by its SH3 domain.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in the membrane tubulation assay and mechanistic understanding.

claim: The WT and Q540H BIN1 variants efficiently anchor DNM2 to membrane tubules.
source: Furthermore, the WT and the likely benign Q540H variant were capable of efficiently anchoring DNM2 to these membrane tubules.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in the membrane tubulation assay.

claim: The F584S BIN1 variant can recruit DNM2 in cells despite showing no binding to DNM2 in vitro.
source: Unexpectedly, the F584S variant, which showed no binding to DNM2 in vitro could also recruit DNM2 in cells.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations comparing in vitro and cellular assays.

claim: The tubules formed by the F584S BIN1 variant are less polarized and organized than WT.
source: However, the tubules formed by this variant appeared to be less polarized and organized than the WT.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in the membrane tubulation assay.

claim: The Y531S and D537V BIN1 variants show markedly reduced ability to recruit DNM2.
source: In contrast, the Y531S and D537V variants showed markedly reduced ability to recruit DNM2, the same cellular phenotype as previously observed in the case of BIN1 variants that cause CNM (Nicot et al., 2007;⁠ Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in the membrane tubulation assay and comparison to prior studies.

claim: Purified DNM2 interacts with BIN1 SH3 with an apparent dissociation constant of 100 nM.
source: We found that purified DNM2 interacts nearly identically to endogenous DNM2 found in myoblast extract with an apparent dissociation constant of 100 nM (pKapp = 7).
evidence: This is based on experimental titration holdup data.

claim: Endogenous DNM2 in myoblast extract interacts with BIN1 SH3 with an apparent dissociation constant of 100 nM.
source: We found that purified DNM2 interacts nearly identically to endogenous DNM2 found in myoblast extract with an apparent dissociation constant of 100 nM (pKapp = 7).
evidence: This is based on experimental native holdup data.

claim: DNM2 displays partial binding activity with the BIN1 SH3 domain.
source: Interestingly, these titration experiments also revealed that DNM2 displays partial binding activity, i.e. not the entire DNM2 population is capable of interacting with the SH3 domain of BIN1.
evidence: This is based on experimental titration holdup observations.

claim: Native holdup can reliably capture interactions of SH3 domains and determine their steady-state binding constants.
source: Thus, we concluded that nHU could be used to reliably capture interactions of SH3 domains and determine their steady-state binding constants.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the benchmarking experiments comparing purified and endogenous DNM2.

claim: 188 proteins showed statistically significant binding to BIN1 SH3 in the nHU-MS experiment.
source: In our assay, we assayed the binding of 6,357 FL proteins, out of which 188 showed statistically significant binding to BIN1_SH3 displaying apparent dissociation constants in the range of 0.5–34 μM (corresponding to 6.4–4.5 pKapp values).
evidence: This is based on experimental nHU-MS data.

claim: BIN1 SH3 interaction partners display apparent dissociation constants in the range of 0.5–34 μM.
source: In our assay, we assayed the binding of 6,357 FL proteins, out of which 188 showed statistically significant binding to BIN1_SH3 displaying apparent dissociation constants in the range of 0.5–34 μM (corresponding to 6.4–4.5 pKapp values).
evidence: This is based on experimental nHU-MS data.

claim: By combining two nHU experiments, 206 proteins showed significant binding to BIN1 SH3.
source: By combining the results of the two experiments, we assayed the binding of 6,453 FL endogenous proteins, out of which 206 showed significant binding to BIN1.
evidence: This is based on combined experimental nHU-MS data from two independent experiments.

claim: AMPH SH3 and ARHGEF7 SH3 show similar affinity profiles to BIN1 SH3 with statistically significant correlation.
source: Based on affinities of the shared partners, AMPH_SH3 and ARHGEF7_SH3 show similar affinity profiles to BIN1_SH3 with statistically significant correlation.
evidence: This is based on comparative analysis of nHU-MS data for different SH3 domains.

claim: ABL1 SH3 and PRMT2 SH3 show affinity profiles that differ substantially from BIN1 SH3 with no significant correlation.
source: In contrast, the affinities of the shared partners between BIN1_SH3 and ABL1_SH3 or PRMT2_SH3 differ substantially with no significant correlation.
evidence: This is based on comparative analysis of nHU-MS data for different SH3 domains.

claim: Only three previously known BIN1 partners (DNM2, ITCH, SMCHD1) were found in the nHU assay.
source: Only three of these partners were previously found to bind BIN1 in high-throughput qualitative interactomic studies: DNM2, ITCH, and SMCHD1.
evidence: This is based on comparison of nHU-MS results with prior literature.

claim: Eight BIN1 SH3 interaction partners (ATXN2, DNM2, DNMT1, MORC2, MTPAP, SBF1, SMCHD1, SPAST) are encoded by genes listed in the gene table of monogenic neuromuscular disorders.
source: Eight proteins (ATXN2, DNM2, DNMT1, MORC2, MTPAP, SBF1, SMCHD1, SPAST) are, like BIN1 itself, encoded by genes listed in the gene table of monogenic neuromuscular disorders (Cohen et al., 2021)⁠.
evidence: This is based on comparison of nHU-MS results with a gene table from a cited reference.

claim: MTMR1 is a close paralog of myotubularin (MTM1) whose mutation can cause X-linked centronuclear myopathy.
source: Another significant BIN1_SH3 binder detected by our assay is MTMR1, a close paralog of myotubularin (MTM1) whose mutation can cause the X-linked form of CNM also called myotubular myopathy (Laporte et al., 1996; Zanoteli et al., 2005).
evidence: This genetic relationship is supported by citations.

claim: DNM2, SMCHD1, DNMT1, MORC2, and SBF1 display relatively high affinity for BIN1 SH3 with dissociation constant <10 μM.
source: Five out of these phenotypically-related partners (DNM2, SMCHD1, DNMT1, MORC2, and SBF1) were found to display relatively high affinity for BIN1_SH3 with a dissociation constant <10 μM (pKd >5), while ATXN2, SPAST, MTMR1, and MTPAP showed somewhat weaker affinities.
evidence: This is based on experimental nHU-MS affinity measurements.

claim: 65% of BIN1 interaction partners contain putative PRMs, indicating >2.5-fold enrichment compared to random occurrence.
source: When we screened the sequences of all identified interaction partners looking for putative PRMs, we could identify such motifs in 65% of the interaction partners of BIN1 (133 out of 206), indicating a >2.5-fold enrichment compared to the random occurrence (Figure 3, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis of nHU-MS results.

claim: 417 putative PRMs were identified within disordered regions of BIN1 interaction partners.
source: Within disordered regions of these proteins, we identified 417 putative PRMs matching the [RK]..P..P or P..P.[RK] consensus motifs (class 1 and class 2 PxxP motifs, respectively).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatic analysis of protein sequences.

claim: 176 motifs out of 448 synthesized PRMs showed detectable binding with BIN1 SH3.
source: All putative PRMs were synthesized as 15-mer biotinylated peptides and their affinities were systematically measured against the SH3 domain of BIN1. Out of these, 176 motifs showed detectable binding with BIN1 (Figure 5A, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on experimental fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: 92 out of 133 BIN1 interaction partners containing PRMs were matched with at least one quantified site-specific affinity.
source: Therefore, out of 133 interaction partners of BIN1_SH3 that contain putative PRMs, we matched 92 with at least one quantified site-specific affinity, annotating nearly half of all identified BIN1_SH3 partners as a likely direct interaction partner of BIN1.
evidence: This is based on combined analysis of nHU-MS and fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: There is poor correlation (PCC of 0.2) between measured affinities of intact proteins and affinities of isolated motifs.
source: Surprisingly, we find a very poor correlation, with a PCC of 0.2, between measured affinities of intact proteins and the affinities of isolated motifs, even if we only consider the best motif in each protein.
evidence: This is based on comparative analysis of nHU-MS and fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: >85% of BIN1 partners bind stronger as intact proteins compared to any isolated PRM in their sequence.
source: Moreover, when we systematically compare these affinity differences, we find that >85% of partners bind stronger as an intact protein compared to any isolated PRM that we could identify in their sequence.
evidence: This is based on comparative analysis of nHU-MS and fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: Most isolated PRMs bind at least five- to sixfold weaker than the full-length protein.
source: These differences are often quite substantial, with a mean/median pKapp (intact protein) - pKd (PRM) difference of 0.71/0.76, meaning that most isolated motifs bind at least five- to sixfold weaker than the full-length protein.
evidence: This is based on comparative analysis of nHU-MS and fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: BIN1 SH3 has a clear preference for class 2 PxxP motifs over class 1 motifs.
source: By comparing the PRM-binding affinities of the SH3 domain of BIN1 with the corresponding affinities of the five other SH3 domains addressed in our study, we have found that BIN1_SH3 has a clear preference for class 2 PxxP motifs over class 1 motifs, similarly to the SH3 domains of AMPH and ARHGEF7 (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplements 1–2, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on comparative analysis of fragmentomic holdup data for multiple SH3 domains.

claim: ABL1 SH3 and OBSCN SH3 prefer class 1 PxxP motifs.
source: In contrast, PRMT2_SH3 does not appear to have a marked specificity and both ABL1_SH3 and OBSCN_SH3 appear to prefer class 1 PxxP motifs.
evidence: This is based on analysis of fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: The affinity profile of BIN1 SH3 is most similar to AMPH SH3.
source: In addition, the affinity profile of BIN1_SH3 was most similar to the affinity profile of AMPH_SH3, and was also similar to the affinity profile of ARHGEF7_SH3, but was more distinct from the affinity profiles of PRMT2_SH3 or ABL1_SH3.
evidence: This is based on comparative analysis of fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: OBSCN SH3 only mediates detectable binding to a handful of PRMs.
source: The SH3 domain of OBSCN was found to only mediate detectable binding to a handful of PRMs included in our panel signifying its peculiar nature compared to the other SH3 domains.
evidence: This is based on fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: BIN1 partners are most often involved in nuclear processes or mitotic processes.
source: This revealed that the identified partners of the SH3 domain of BIN1 are most often involved in two types of biological processes, either related to nuclear processes (such as DNA replication or mRNA processing) or to mitotic processes.
evidence: This is based on functional enrichment analysis of nHU-MS results.

claim: PRC1 was identified as a partner of BIN1 SH3 displaying medium affinity in the nHU screen.
source: PRC1 was originally identified as a partner of the SH3 domain of BIN1 in our proteome-wide nHU interactomic screen displaying a medium affinity.
evidence: This is based on experimental nHU-MS data.

claim: Two potential PRMs in PRC1 both display binding activity to BIN1 SH3 with comparable affinities to full-length PRC1.
source: Later, we identified two potential PRMs in its sequence that both displayed binding activity to the SH3 domain of BIN1 with comparable affinities to the full-length PRC1 (Figure 5).
evidence: This is based on fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: The tandem PRMs of PRC1 overlap with mitotic phosphorylation sites and a nuclear localization signal.
source: Interestingly, these tandem PRMs of PRC1 overlap with mitotic phosphorylation sites and a previously characterized nuclear localization signal that regulates PRC1 localization during the cell cycle (Jiang et al., 1998)⁠.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and a citation to prior literature.

claim: BIN1-induced membrane tubules display dramatic rearrangement during mitosis.
source: Surprisingly, all dividing cells (WT or F584S) either turned out to be completely devoid of BIN1 tubular structures, or the short membrane tubules were restricted to the cell periphery (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in membrane tubulation assays.

claim: In late anaphase and early cytokinesis, BIN1 membrane tubules reappear and are found in higher density around the cleavage furrow and midbody.
source: In late anaphase, and in the early stages of cytokinesis, the membrane tubules reappeared in cells and were found in higher density around the cleavage furrow and the midbody.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in membrane tubulation assays.

claim: PRC1 displays a moderate affinity with BIN1 with an apparent dissociation constant of 1.4 μM.
source: This experiment confirmed this interaction and we have found that PRC1 displayed a moderate affinity with an apparent dissociation constant of 1.4 μM (pKapp = 5.86), which is approximately >10-fold weaker than the BIN1-DNM2 interaction.
evidence: This is based on experimental nHU titration data with myoblast extract.

claim: PRC1 localizes at the nucleus during interphase and translocates to the mitotic spindle midzone during anaphase and to the cleavage furrow and midbody during cytokinesis.
source: Although PRC1 is known to localize at the nucleus during interphase, it translocates to the mitotic spindle midzone during anaphase and at the cleavage furrow and the midbody during cytokinesis (Mollinari et al., 2002)⁠.
evidence: This localization pattern is supported by a citation.

claim: BIN1 and PRC1 are well separated in interphasic cells.
source: As expected, in interphasic cells BIN1 and PRC1 are well separated as PRC1 is only found in the nucleus and BIN1 remains in the cytoplasm at membrane tubules.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in immunofluorescence assays.

claim: Once cells enter mitotic phase, PRC1 localizes to the same cellular regions as BIN1 during anaphase and cytokinesis.
source: Yet, once cells entered the mitotic phase, PRC1 localizes to the same cellular regions as BIN1 during anaphase and cytokinesis, that is cleavage furrow and midbody (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in immunofluorescence assays.

claim: Y531S, D537V, and F584S BIN1 variants cause substantial perturbation in the affinity interactome of BIN1.
source: We found that only those variants caused substantial perturbation in the affinity interactome of BIN1 that we also identified as a perturbing variants with our conventional screening (Figure 2).
evidence: This is based on fragmentomic holdup data measuring affinity interactomes of variants.

claim: Y531S and D537V BIN1 variants cause perturbed affinity profiles with general affinity interactome reshuffling.
source: Both Y531S, D537V cause perturbed affinity profiles (PAP) with a general affinity interactome reshuffling, in which most peptide targets mediate weaker affinities compared to the WT SH3 domain.
evidence: This is based on fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: F584S BIN1 variant causes a near complete loss of function.
source: In contrast, the mutation F584S causes a near complete loss of function (LOF).
evidence: This is based on fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: The common variant T532M displays an affinity interactome quasi identical to WT BIN1.
source: In support of this, the common variant T532M, that displays affinity interactome quasi identical to WT BIN1, is present 116 times at homozygous state in genomic databases with no connection to any clinical phenotype (Karczewski et al., 2020)⁠.
evidence: This is based on fragmentomic holdup data and comparison with genomic databases.

claim: Y531 and D537 are positioned near the PRM binding interface of BIN1 SH3.
source: D537 and Y531 are positioned near the PRM binding interface, F584 is buried in the hydrophobic core of the SH3 domain.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis using AlphaFold2 predictions.

claim: F584 is buried in the hydrophobic core of the BIN1 SH3 domain.
source: D537 and Y531 are positioned near the PRM binding interface, F584 is buried in the hydrophobic core of the SH3 domain.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis using AlphaFold2 predictions.

claim: Y531S and D537V variants likely impact PRM binding in a direct manner.
source: Thus, it is likely that the Y531S and D537V variants impact the PRM binding in a direct manner and the F584S variant causes a destabilized SH3 fold.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural positions of the variants and their effects on binding.

claim: F584S variant likely causes a destabilized SH3 fold.
source: Thus, it is likely that the Y531S and D537V variants impact the PRM binding in a direct manner and the F584S variant causes a destabilized SH3 fold.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural position of the variant and its effects on binding.

claim: The in vitro destabilization of F584S can be partially rescued in the context of full-length BIN1, possibly by intramolecular interactions.
source: Since this variant was found to be capable of recruiting DNM2 in cellular assays, it is likely that this in vitro destabilization can be partially rescued in the context of full-length BIN1, possibly by intramolecular interactions with other regions of the protein (Kojima et al., 2004; Wu and Baumgart, 2014)⁠.
evidence: This is inferred from the discrepancy between in vitro and cellular results, supported by citations.

claim: AlphaFold2 Multimer predicted no obvious indication of perturbed affinity interactomes for Y531S, D537V, and F584S variants.
source: The resulting models all predicted complexes that made structural sense with no obvious indication of their perturbed affinity interactomes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on structural predictions using AlphaFold2.

claim: Standard modern structure-prediction tools are not yet fully capable of foreseeing the consequences of sequence variants.
source: Thus, we concluded that standard modern structure-prediction tools are not yet fully capable of foreseeing the consequences of sequence variants.
evidence: This is inferred from the inability of AlphaFold2 to predict the observed affinity perturbations.

claim: Experimental approaches such as holdup assays are essential to accurately measure the consequences of missense variants.
source: Therefore, experimental approaches, such as the holdup assays are still going to be essential to accurately measure the consequences of missense variants.
evidence: This is inferred from the limitations of structure prediction tools.

claim: BIN1 expression fluctuates throughout the cell cycle similarly to other regulators of the cell cycle.
source: Both proteomic and transcriptomic data showed that BIN1 expression fluctuates throughout the cell cycle similarly to other regulators of the cell cycle, albeit to a more modest extent (Santos et al., 2015)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: DNM2 co-localizes with microtubule bundles formed at the midbody.
source: It has been also showed that DNM2 co-localizes with microtubule bundles formed at the midbody (Thompson et al., 2002)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: PRC1 cross-links microtubule bundles at the midbody to promote division of daughter cells.
source: During cytokinesis, PRC1, a new partner of BIN1 identified here, is known to cross-link microtubule bundles at the midbody to promote the division of the daughter cells (Mollinari et al., 2002)⁠.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: BIN1 is involved in the regulation of cytokinesis.
source: Our study demonstrates, that BIN1 is also involved in this process, where it is likely that the membrane remodeling activities of the BAR domain of BIN1 is mediating regulatory functions.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations and inference from the data.

claim: DNM2 ranks among the highest affinity interactions of BIN1.
source: We could confirm that DNM2 ranks among the highest affinity interactions of BIN1, signifying the importance of this interaction.
evidence: This is based on experimental nHU-MS affinity measurements.

claim: SMCHD1 is a strong interaction partner of BIN1, displaying similar affinity as DNM2.
source: For example, we identified SMCHD1 as a strong interaction partner of BIN1, displaying a similar affinity as DNM2.
evidence: This is based on experimental nHU-MS affinity measurements.

claim: Mutations of SMCHD1 are linked to facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD).
source: Mutations of this protein are also linked to a neuromuscular disorder called facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) and both FSHD and CNM patients suffer from muscle weakness as a major symptom (Cohen et al., 2021)⁠.
evidence: This genetic association is supported by a citation.

claim: Both FSHD and CNM patients suffer from muscle weakness as a major symptom.
source: Mutations of this protein are also linked to a neuromuscular disorder called facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) and both FSHD and CNM patients suffer from muscle weakness as a major symptom (Cohen et al., 2021)⁠.
evidence: This clinical observation is supported by a citation.

claim: The BIN1-SMCHD1 complex may play a role in the symptomatic manifestations of both FSHD and CNM.
source: Our unbiased study suggests that their complex may play a role in the symptomatic manifestations of both conditions.
evidence: This is speculated based on the identified interaction and shared symptoms.

claim: Disruptive mutations in the SH3 domain of BIN1 will perturb all identified interactions that collectively contribute to CNM.
source: Nevertheless, even if the impact of the newly discovered BIN1 interaction partners will turn out to be somewhat less critical than DNM2 in CNM, disruptive mutations in the SH3 domain of BIN1 will necessarily perturb all the identified interactions that collectively contribute to CNM.
evidence: This is inferred from the observed proteome-wide affinity perturbations caused by BIN1 variants.

claim: Affinity interactomic approaches allow investigation of consequences of naturally occurring variants in a highly quantitative manner.
source: Affinity interactomic approaches allow the investigation of the consequences of naturally occurring variants in a highly quantitative manner (Weimer et al., 2023)⁠.
evidence: This capability is supported by a citation.

claim: Most BIN1 SH3 variants do not cause detectable perturbation in the intrinsic affinity interactome of BIN1.
source: Using our approach, we could demonstrate that most of these variants do not cause detectable perturbation in the intrinsic affinity interactome of BIN1, but we could also identify three rare variants that caused affinity rewiring, leading to altered molecular phenotypes related to BIN1.
evidence: This is based on fragmentomic holdup data for multiple variants.

claim: Three rare BIN1 variants (Y531S, D537V, F584S) cause affinity rewiring leading to altered molecular phenotypes.
source: Using our approach, we could demonstrate that most of these variants do not cause detectable perturbation in the intrinsic affinity interactome of BIN1, but we could also identify three rare variants that caused affinity rewiring, leading to altered molecular phenotypes related to BIN1.
evidence: This is based on fragmentomic holdup data.

claim: Affinity interactomics can associate rare variants with putative clinical risk even when genetic approaches cannot determine statistically significant causality.
source: Although genetic approaches could not determine statistically significant causality between these mutations and the pathology due to their sparsity, our affinity interactomic approach has associated them with putative clinical risk.
evidence: This is inferred from the ability to detect molecular phenotypes for rare variants.

claim: Affinity interactomics is suitable for testing effects of sequence variations to identify and validate potentially disease-causing mutations.
source: In conclusion, we demonstrated that affinity interactomics is not limited to the identification and characterization of interaction partners, but is also suitable for testing effects of sequence variations in order to identify and validate potentially disease-causing mutations.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the demonstrated applications in the study.

claim: The study identified hundreds of new BIN1 interaction partners proteome-wide.
source: We identified hundreds of new BIN1 interaction partners proteome-wide, among which many appear to participate in cell division, suggesting a critical role of BIN1 in the regulation of mitosis.
evidence: This is based on experimental nHU-MS data.

claim: Many BIN1 interaction partners participate in cell division, suggesting a critical role of BIN1 in the regulation of mitosis.
source: We identified hundreds of new BIN1 interaction partners proteome-wide, among which many appear to participate in cell division, suggesting a critical role of BIN1 in the regulation of mitosis.
evidence: This is inferred from functional enrichment analysis of nHU-MS results.

claim: BIN1 mutations cause proteome-wide affinity perturbation.
source: Finally, we show that the identified BIN1 mutations indeed cause proteome-wide affinity perturbation, signifying the importance of employing unbiased affinity interactomic approaches.
evidence: This is based on fragmentomic holdup data for BIN1 variants.
